এস,আর,ও নং- ১৭৪-আইন/২০১৬/৩৬/কাস্টমস।— Customs Act, 1969 (Act No. IV of 1969) এর section 219(1), THIRD SCHEDULE এর item 21 এর সহিত পঠিতব্য, এ প্রদত্ত ক্ষমতাবলে জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ড, নিম্নরূপ বিধিমালা প্রণয়ন করিল, যথা :-

Customs Act 1969: This act provides the enabling authority under Section 219(1) for the government to frame rules regarding customs agents.
Third Schedule: This schedule provides the legislative support, specifically through its item 21, for the issuance of rules governing customs procedures.
National Board of Revenue: The board is the authorized body empowered to frame and enact the Customs Agent Licensing Rules under the authority of the Customs Act.

processed_clauses.resolved_text: ১। সংক্ষিপ্ত শিরোনাম।— এই বিধিমালা কাস্টমস এজেন্ট লাইসেন্সিং বিধিমালা, ২০১৬ নামে অভিহিত হইবে।

Customs Agents Licensing Rules 2016: This clause provides the official short title of the rules, identifying them as the Customs Agents Licensing Rules 2016.

Customs Act 1969: This law is formally referred to as the Act within these rules, establishing the legal framework for customs administration in Bangladesh.
Customs Agent: A customs agent is defined as any person or organization that performs tasks related to the entry or exit of vehicles, or the import or export of goods and baggage at a customs station, as intended under the relevant section of the Customs Act 1969.
Customs Broker: Refers to the formal role defined under these rules, which governs those authorized to handle customs-related documentation and procedures on behalf of others.
Customs Station: A customs station is defined in accordance with the specific definition provided under the Customs Act 1969.
Customs House: A custom house is defined as an facility declared and authorized under the relevant section of the Customs Act 1969.
Company: Refers to a business entity as defined under the specific section of the Companies Act 1994.
Importer and Exporter: Defined as a person or institution involved in the importation of goods from abroad or the exportation of goods to other countries.
Form: Refers to the official documents appended to these rules that must be utilized for procedural compliance.
Partnership Act 1932: This Act provides the legal definition for a firm for the purposes of these licensing rules.
National Board of Revenue: Identified as the Board within these rules, as defined under the Customs Act 1969.
Reference License: A license issued under the specific rule of this framework to provide authorization for designated customs-related activities.
Licensee: Authorization granted under these rules to an entity enabling them to operate as a customs agent.
Licensing Authority: The body constituted under these rules responsible for the issuance and oversight of customs agent licenses.

processed_clauses.resolved_text:
৩। লাইসেন্সিং কর্তৃপক্ষ।— (১) লাইসেন্সিং কর্তৃপক্ষ কাস্টমস এজেন্ট লাইসেন্স প্রদান করিবে।
(২) উপ-বিধি (১) এর উদ্দেশ্যপূরণকল্পে নিম্নবর্ণিত কর্মকর্তাগণের সমন্বয়ে লাইসেন্সিং কর্তৃপক্ষ গঠিত হইবে, যথা:-
(ক) কাস্টম হাউসে কর্মরত একজন অতিরিক্ত কমিশনার এবং একজন ডেপুটি কমিশনার; অথবা
(খ) কাস্টম হাউসে অতিরিক্ত কমিশনার না থাকিলে একজন যুগ্ম কমিশনার এবং একজন সহকারী কমিশনার।
(৩) উপ-বিধি (২) এর দফা (ক) এর ক্ষেত্রে অতিরিক্ত কমিশনার সভাপতি ও ডেপুটি কমিশনার সদস্য-সচিব হইবেন এবং দফা (খ) এর ক্ষেত্রে যুগ্ম-কমিশনার সভাপতি এবং সহকারী কমিশনার সদস্য-সচিব হইবেন।

Licensing Authority: The Licensing Authority is responsible for the issuance of Customs Agent licenses.

The composition of the Licensing Authority is structured based on the available customs officers at the customs house, consisting of a combination of either an Additional Commissioner and a Deputy Commissioner or a Joint Commissioner and an Assistant Commissioner.
The Licensing Authority functions with the senior officer serving as the chairperson and the junior officer serving as the member-secretary.
Customs Agent License: A license required for the operation of customs agents is issued by the designated Licensing Authority.
Customs House: The Customs House serves as the administrative location where the Licensing Authority is constituted and operates from.

processed_clauses.resolved_text:
৪। লাইসেন্স প্রদানে বোর্ডের পূর্বানুমতি।— (১) লাইসেন্সিং কর্তৃপক্ষ লাইসেন্স প্রদান করিবার পূর্বে সংশ্লিষ্ট কাস্টমস স্টেশনের বিদ্যমান লাইসেন্স সংখ্যা, বিগত ৫ (পাঁচ) বৎসরের আমদানি-রপ্তানির পরিসংখ্যান এবং নূতন লাইসেন্স প্রদানের যৌক্তিকতা উল্লেখপূর্বক অনুমতি গ্রহণের জন্য বোর্ডে লিখিতভাবে আবেদন করিবে।
(২) বোর্ড উপ-বিধি (১) এর অধীন আবেদন প্রাপ্তির পর উহা যাচাই-বাছাইপূর্বক লাইসেন্স প্রদানের যৌক্তিকতা বিবেচনা করিয়া সংশ্লিষ্ট কাস্টম হাউসকে লাইসেন্স প্রদানের অনুমতি প্রদান করিবে।

National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is the authority responsible for reviewing and granting prior approval for the issuance of new licenses based on official requests.
Upon receiving a request from the licensing authority, the Board must evaluate the justification and statistics provided to determine whether to authorize the issuance of a new license.
Customs Agent License: The licensing authority is required to obtain prior written approval from the National Board of Revenue before issuing new licenses.

The application for approval must include details such as the existing number of licenses at the relevant customs station, import and export statistics from the preceding five-year period, and a justification for the new license.
Customs House: The Customs House receives the authorization from the National Board of Revenue to proceed with the issuance of a license after the Board has vetted the justification for the request.

National Board of Revenue: The licensing authority must obtain permission from the Board before initiating the customs agent licensing process.
The Board has the power to grant an extension of time for the licensing authority to issue a license if it fails to meet the initial deadline.
Customs Act 1969: Applicants must demonstrate practical knowledge of the Customs Act 1969, among other relevant laws, as part of the licensing requirements.
Tax Identification Number: An applicant is required to submit a valid electronic Taxpayer Identification Number certificate as part of the mandatory documentation for a customs agent license.
Partnership Act 1932: If an applicant is a partnership firm, they must submit a certified copy of the partnership deed as required by the Partnership Act 1932.
Customs Agent License: The licensing authority follows a structured procedure including application submission, document verification, examination, and fee payment to issue a license.
Applicants must provide proof of professional qualifications, financial solvency, and various corporate or personal legal documents to be eligible for the license.
The licensing authority may reject an application for valid reasons, providing written notice to the applicant within a specified timeframe.

processed_clauses.clause_title: নিজস্ব পণ্য খালাসের (Self Clearance) জন্য লাইসেন্স প্রদান
processed_clauses.resolved_text: ৬। নিজস্ব পণ্য খালাসের (Self Clearance) জন্য লাইসেন্স প্রদান।— কোন ব্যক্তি তদকর্তৃক আমদানিকৃত বা রপ্তানিযোগ্য পণ্য নিজস্ব প্রতিষ্ঠানের মাধ্যমে খালাস করিবার জন্য এই বিধিমালার অধীন লাইসেন্স প্রাপ্তির সকল শর্ত পূরণপূর্বক আবেদন করিলে লাইসেন্সিং কর্তৃপক্ষ যাচাই-বাছাইপূর্বক বিধি ৫ অনুসারে শুধুমাত্র নিজস্ব প্রতিষ্ঠানের পণ্য খালাসের জন্য ফরম ‘খ’ অনুযায়ী আবেদনকারীকে লাইসেন্স প্রদান করিবে।

Self-Clearance License: This license allows an entity to clear their own imported or exported goods through their own internal organization rather than through a third party. Applicants must fulfill all specified regulatory conditions before the licensing authority conducts a review to grant the license using the prescribed form.
Customs Clearance Procedure: The process for obtaining a self-clearance license requires the applicant to submit a formal request that undergoes examination by the licensing authority to ensure compliance with all procedural rules.

processed_clauses.resolved_text: ৭। লাইসেন্সের মেয়াদ।— এই বিধিমালার অধীন প্রদত্ত লাইসেন্সের মেয়াদ হইবে লাইসেন্স প্রদানের তারিখ হইতে পরবর্তী ৫ (পাঁচ) বৎসর।

Customs Clearing and Forwarding Agent: The license issued under these rules is valid for a fixed duration of five years, starting from the date of issuance.

processed_clauses.resolved_text:
৮। লাইসেন্স প্রদানের ক্ষেত্রে বিধি-নিষেধ।— এই বিধিমালার অন্যান্য বিধিতে যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন, সম্পূর্ণ বিদেশী মালিকানাধীন কোন প্রতিষ্ঠানকে এই বিধিমালার আওতায় লাইসেন্স প্রদান করা যাইবে না :
তবে শর্ত থাকে যে, দেশী ও বিদেশী যৌথ মালিকানায় প্রতিষ্ঠিত কোম্পানি লাইসেন্স পাইবার যোগ্য হইবে, যদি বিদেশী মালিক বা মালিকদের শেয়ার ধারণের পরিমাণ উক্ত কোম্পানির মোট শেয়ারের শতকরা ৪০ (চল্লিশ) এর অধিক না হয়।

Customs Clearing and Forwarding Agent: A foreign-owned entity is strictly prohibited from being granted a license under these rules.
A company with joint domestic and foreign ownership is eligible for a license, provided that the foreign equity stake does not exceed a specified percentage of the total shares.

Customs Agent: A Customs Agent must apply for license renewal at least a specified number of working days before the current license expires.
The application for renewal requires payment of a specific fee, submission of various documents such as trade licenses and tax certificates, and proof of association membership.

If a Customs Agent fails to apply within the mandatory timeframe, they may request an extension from the licensing authority by providing valid reasons, which can be granted for a limited total period.
Renewal of a license is contingent upon the Customs Agent's past performance, legal compliance, and absence of outstanding government dues or customs-related cases.

The licensing authority may refuse to renew a license if the agent is deemed high-risk due to involvement in unlawful shipments or false declarations, or if their knowledge of tax and customs regulations is found to be unsatisfactory.
Licensing Authority: The licensing authority is responsible for receiving renewal applications, verifying documents, and assessing the past performance of the Customs Agent.
The authority has the discretion to grant limited extensions for renewal applications if the agent fails to apply on time and provides a satisfactory explanation.
Upon approval, the licensing authority must renew the license for a period of five years within a set timeframe after receiving the application.

If the licensing authority decides not to renew a license based on non-compliance or unsatisfactory performance, it must formally notify the Customs Agent in writing within a specified number of working days.
Customs Act 1969: The Customs Act 1969 serves as the legal framework for identifying high-risk agents, particularly those found to be involved in illegal clearances or the submission of false declarations.
Value Added Tax Act 1991: The licensing authority evaluates the Customs Agent's practical experience and compliance with the Value Added Tax Act 1991 as part of the criteria for license renewal.

processed_clauses.resolved_text: ১০। লাইসেন্সের অধিক্ষেত্র।— এই বিধিমালার অধীন প্রদত্ত লাইসেন্সের অধিক্ষেত্র হইবে লাইসেন্সে উল্লিখিত সংশ্লিষ্ট কাস্টমস বন্দর, কাস্টম হাউস বা কাস্টমস স্টেশন।

Customs Clearing and Forwarding Agent: The jurisdictional scope of a license granted under these rules is limited to the specific customs port, custom house, or customs station explicitly mentioned in the license document.

processed_clauses.resolved_text:
১১। রেফারেন্স লাইসেন্স।— কোন কাস্টমস এজেন্ট মূল লাইসেন্সে উল্লিখিত কাস্টমস স্টেশন ব্যতীত অন্য কোন কাস্টমস স্টেশনের রেফারেন্স লাইসেন্স প্রাপ্তির জন্য মূল লাইসেন্সের কপি এবং বিধি ৫ এ বর্ণিত দলিলাদিসহ ফরম-গ অনুযায়ী আবেদন করিতে পারিবে এবং লাইসেন্সিং কর্তৃপক্ষ উক্ত দলিলাদি যাচাই-বাছাইপূর্বক আবেদনকারীর মৌখিক পরীক্ষা গ্রহণের মাধ্যমে রেফারেন্স লাইসেন্স প্রদান করিতে পারিবে :
তবে শর্ত থাকে যে, কাস্টমস এজেন্ট এর ন্যূনতম ১০ (দশ) বৎসরের সন্তোষজনক কার্যক্রম পরিচালনা করিবার অভিজ্ঞতা থাকিলে বিধি ৫ এর দফা (২) এর উপ-দফা (৭) প্রযোজ্য হইবে না।

Customs Agent: A Customs Agent may apply for a reference license to operate at a customs station other than the one specified in their original license by submitting the required documentation and form.
Customs Agents with a specified number of years of satisfactory operational experience are exempt from certain documentary requirements when applying for a reference license.
Reference License: A reference license allows a Customs Agent to perform professional activities at a customs station that is not covered by their primary license.
The issuance of a reference license by the licensing authority is subject to the verification of submitted documents and the successful completion of an oral examination by the applicant.
Licensing Authority: The licensing authority is responsible for verifying the application documents and conducting an oral assessment for Customs Agents seeking a reference license.

processed_clauses.resolved_text:
১২। লাইসেন্সের অনুলিপি প্রদান।— (১) লাইসেন্স হারাইয়া গেলে বা যে কোন প্রকারে নষ্ট হইয়া গেলে সংশ্লিষ্ট কাস্টমস এজেন্ট ২,৫০০/- (দুই হাজার পাঁচশত) টাকা ফি পরিশোধপূর্বক লিখিত আবেদন করিলে লাইসেন্সিং কর্তৃপক্ষ লাইসেন্সের একটি অবিকল নকল প্রদান করিবে।
(২) এই বিধিমালার অধীন প্রদত্ত লাইসেন্স হারাইয়া গেলে সংশ্লিষ্ট থানায় সাধারণ ডায়েরী করিতে হইবে এবং উহার একটি অনুলিপি আবেদনের সহিত দাখিল করিতে হইবে।

Customs Agent License: A customs agent whose license is lost or destroyed can obtain a duplicate copy by submitting a formal written application to the licensing authority.
The issuance of a duplicate license requires the payment of a specified fee as prescribed by the relevant rules.
Customs Agent: In the event of a lost or destroyed license, the agent is required to file a general diary at the local police station and submit a copy of this report along with the application for a duplicate license.
Licensing Authority: The licensing authority is empowered to issue a duplicate license upon receiving a valid written request and the necessary application fee from the agent.

processed_clauses.clause_title: লাইসেন্সের গঠনগত পরিবর্তন বা হস্তান্তরের ক্ষেত্রে বিধি-নিষেধ

Customs Agent License: The license is generally non-transferable and restricted from structural changes unless specific regulatory conditions are met.
Failure by a legal heir to notify or apply for the transfer of a license within the specified timeframe following the death of the licensee results in the automatic cancellation of the license.
Partnership Act 1932: A licensee may undergo a structural change to become a partnership firm under this Act, provided they obtain approval from the licensing authorities and the partners successfully pass the required qualification examination.
Companies Act 1994: A licensee may undergo a structural change to become a company under this Act, provided they obtain approval from the licensing authorities and the directors successfully pass the required qualification examination.
Licensing Authority: The authority must approve any structural changes to a license, such as conversion into a partnership or company.
The authority oversees the transfer process for legal heirs following the death of a licensee, including conducting qualification examinations and reviewing applications within a specified timeframe.

processed_clauses.clause_title: কাস্টমস এজেন্ট এর দায়িত্ব ও কর্তব্য

Customs Agent: A Customs Agent is required to submit their authorization letter from the client to the relevant customs authority.
They must verify client documents, prepare and submit accurate Bills of Entry or Bills of Export, and ensure all required customs declaration forms are filed according to the Valuation Rules.
Customs Agents are obligated to notify customs authorities in writing if they discover that a client has provided false information or failed to comply with the law.
They must collect government dues from clients and deposit them into the state treasury promptly, and conversely, pass on any refunds received from the government to the client without delay.

Customs Agents are prohibited from exerting undue influence on customs officials, accessing customs records without permission, employing individuals whose licenses were previously rejected or cancelled, or engaging in financial transactions like lending money to customs officials.
They must maintain all transaction records, bills, and correspondence for a minimum period of three years and ensure these records are made available to customs officers upon request.

Customs Agents are responsible for maintaining a professional standard of knowledge, skill, and integrity while providing maximum cooperation to the customs authorities in the discharge of their duties.
Bill of Entry: Customs Agents must submit the Bill of Entry via electronic or manual methods, as applicable, accompanied by all necessary supporting documentation and valuation declarations.
Bill of Export: Customs Agents must submit the Bill of Export via electronic or manual methods, as applicable, accompanied by all necessary supporting documentation.
Customs Valuation (Determination of Valu: The declaration of value for customs purposes must be carried out in accordance with the provisions specified in these rules.
Customs Authority: Customs authorities have the right to request documents from a Customs Agent, and agents are prohibited from concealing, removing, or destroying such requested records.

processed_clauses.resolved_text: ১৫। স্বাক্ষর প্রদানের ক্ষমতা।— লাইসেন্সিং কর্তৃপক্ষের অনুমোদনক্রমে কাস্টমস এজেন্ট তাহার পক্ষে কাস্টমস সংক্রান্ত দলিলপত্রে স্বাক্ষর করিবার জন্য এক বা একাধিক ব্যক্তিকে ফরম-ছ এর নমুনা অনুযায়ী দলিল স্বাক্ষরের ক্ষমতা অর্পণ করিতে পারিবেন।

Customs Agent: A customs agent is authorized to delegate the power to sign customs-related documentation to one or more individuals.
The delegation of signing authority must be performed according to the sample provided in the prescribed form and requires approval from the licensing authority.
Licensing Authority: The licensing authority is responsible for providing the necessary approval before a customs agent can delegate signing authority to other individuals.

Customs Agent: A Customs Agent is authorized to appoint a Customs Sarkar to conduct customs clearance activities on their behalf.
The Customs Agent must submit an application with required documentation to the licensing authority to obtain a permit for their appointed Customs Sarkar.

Customs Agent: A customs agent is required to maintain professional conduct and perform duties in accordance with customs house regulations.

Customs Agents Licensing Rules 2016: This set of rules establishes the regulatory framework for granting, renewing, suspending, or cancelling licenses for clearing, forwarding, and shipping agents. It mandates the specific form and procedural requirements under which these operations must be conducted at customs houses or customs stations.
Customs Act 1969: Section 207 of this Act provides the primary legal authority for the licensing and regulation of customs agents in Bangladesh.
Customs Agent License: This license is issued under the authority of the Customs Agents Licensing Rules 2016 for conducting clearing, forwarding, and shipping agency business at a designated customs house or station.
The license is non-transferable and remains valid for a fixed duration of five years from the date of issue, provided it is not cancelled, suspended, or denied renewal for regulatory violations.

Customs Agent: A customs agent is required to formally authorize specific representatives, such as assistants or clerks, to perform operational duties on behalf of their firm.
The authorized representative is empowered to sign customs documents, handle manifests, process refund or drawback claims, and accept payments or acknowledge receipts on behalf of the principal.
Customs Documents: Documents such as bills of entry and bills of export are subject to formal signing procedures by authorized representatives of a customs agent.
These documents facilitate the operational customs clearance process for imports and exports.
Licensing Authority: The licensing authority is the recipient of the formal letter of authorization submitted by a customs agent to designate representatives for operational duties.
Customs Agent Representation Authorizati: The principal firm assumes full legal responsibility and liability for all actions and signatures performed by their designated representatives in the course of customs business.
The process requires the submission of specimen signatures of all authorized representatives to the relevant customs authorities for verification and record-keeping.
